title: Your first expedition
instruction: Take one lesson at a time. Replay a line, open its screen, or choose Next lesson when you are ready.
text: Welcome, Commander. Your officers will help you learn the controls and plan your first expedition. Starting this tutorial pauses the game. Take your time, replay any lesson, and move on when you are ready. You remain in command of every order.

title: Read the star map
instruction: Use Home to find your starting system. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and select a star to inspect it.
text: Begin with the Home button. Drag the map to look around, and use the mouse wheel to zoom. Select a star to inspect what we know. A bright, large marker is not proof of a giant star. Read its known classification in the system details.

title: Control the clock
instruction: Space pauses or resumes. Use the clock control for faster simulation during long waits. Pause again before an important decision.
text: Time is under your control. Press Space to pause or resume the simulation. The clock control changes the running speed. Use faster speeds during long waits, then pause to review a new report. Opening an operations page does not automatically pause the game.

title: Check what we can afford
instruction: Review cash, income, operating costs and reserves before committing to a project.
text: Before we expand, review the economy. Cash pays for commitments and ongoing operations. Stored materials are a separate requirement. Check our income and running costs as well as the price of a new project. A project we can begin may still need funding while it operates.

title: Build the foundations
instruction: Inspect an available project and its requirements. The First Light guide shows the construction currently needed for the opening.
text: Construction turns stored materials and time into working infrastructure. Open a project and read its requirements before placing an order. The First Light guide identifies the infrastructure needed for our next objective. Research and construction can run together, provided both have the support they need.

title: Choose a research project
instruction: Inspect an available research project. Read its requirements, costs and purpose before starting it.
text: Research opens new possibilities, but each project has requirements. Select an available project and read what it investigates, what it costs, and what support it needs. Starting research is not the same as completing it. Watch its progress, and use the First Light guide to plan toward warp flight.

title: Follow the opening objective
instruction: Read the live research and construction suggestions. Return here when you are unsure what to do next.
text: The First Light guide updates as our civilization develops. Its current objective connects research, construction, and the next useful capability. Follow those live suggestions rather than expecting a single button to unlock interstellar travel. If a project is blocked, inspect its missing requirement and address that first.

title: Build a useful fleet
instruction: Inspect scout, science and colony designs. Build only when the listed facilities, capabilities, materials and funding are ready.
text: Different ships have different jobs. A scout investigates a route, a science vessel conducts detailed surveys, and a colony ship carries settlers. Open Ships and inspect the available designs. Check their requirements and costs. An accepted construction order still needs time before a ship joins the fleet.

title: Send a scout
instruction: Once a scout exists, select it and review its fuel and mission. On the star map, right-click a destination to issue a travel order.
text: When a scout is ready, select it and check its fuel and current mission. On the star map, right click a destination to request travel. Read any restriction before trying again. A moving ship uses real travel time and fuel. A star on the chart is not yet a fully surveyed system.

title: Learn what is really there
instruction: Use reconnaissance first, then a science mission for detailed survey information. Wait for the actual mission to finish.
text: Reconnaissance and a detailed survey answer different questions. Use a scout to investigate first, then a science vessel for deeper study when the mission becomes available. Wait for the survey report before judging a world's suitability. Information we have not discovered should remain unknown.

title: Choose a place to settle
instruction: Review surveyed colony sites, environmental requirements and the available colony ship. A settlement order must meet the game's listed conditions.
text: A promising world is only the beginning. Review its known environment, the settlement requirements, and the colony ship available to carry our people. Follow the reasons shown if settlement is blocked. After founding a colony, check its food, power, funding, and supply needs so it can sustain itself.

title: Meet other civilizations
instruction: Relations contains known contacts and diplomatic proposals. An empty list can simply mean you have not made contact yet.
text: When we establish contact, Relations becomes our diplomatic workspace. Review the other party and the terms of a proposal before responding. An unidentified signal is not yet a diplomatic relationship. If no contacts appear, continue exploring. There is no need to invent a threat where we have no evidence.

title: Save and continue
instruction: Use Save in the campaign drawer, or press F6. Finish tutorial closes this guide; it does not complete campaign objectives.
text: You have the essentials for your first expedition. Use Save in the campaign controls, or press F six, and check the confirmation. Return to the First Light guide whenever you need the next objective. Finishing these lessons leaves every research project, ship, and settlement in your hands.
